decisionsTitle: A volunteer may be given several roles
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-20**, from his phone, on the «Voluntari» card (§761, in production): «I want to be able to assign multiple roles to a volunteer, to be more flexible». Since §761 the organizers gave each volunteer **one** role (`event_volunteers.role_id`); a person who stands at the start for «Direcționare» and then at kilometre five for the «Punct de hidratare» had to be two rows or one role. Amends §761 (the roles given, the card, the count, the emails, the agreement's blanks, the CSV) and §821 (the public list's role).

**Decision — the data.** A table of its own, `event_volunteer_role_assignments` (migration `0177`, expand only): the volunteer (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), a role of the event (`CASCADE` too, for the reason §761 gave for the choices: an event's delete reaches the rows only through the volunteers' second-level cascade), the moment, the pair the primary key — one row per role given, any of the event's, ticked by the person or not; none for an offer nobody placed («De repartizat»). The migration made every existing `role_id` that volunteer's one assignment (`tests/integration/db/volunteer-role-assignments-migration.test.ts` proves it on PGlite, twice-safe). **`role_id` stays until a later contract release**: nothing reads it any more, and every write of a person's roles mirrors the first of them there (null for none), so the code serving while the migration runs reads a sane value and the column's `RESTRICT` stays true to the assignments — the service refuses deleting a role anybody holds or ticked (`VOLUNTEER_ROLE_HAS_PEOPLE`), so the database's own refusal is never reached. The choices (`event_volunteer_role_choices`) stay what the person offered; the assignments are what the organizers decided.

**«N din M» counts a person on each role given.** Somebody given two roles does both, so each role's standing counts them («Înscris» and «Confirmat», never «Anulat», as before), the public form's «mai e nevoie de N» reads the same, and «Câte ecusoane» starts a role without a number at the people it was given, the same way.

**The card «Voluntari».** A row's roles given are chips under «Roluri date» (the glyph `given`, a word and a glyph, never colour alone), each with **«Ia-i rolul …»** — one plain form posting that role (`unassignVolunteerAction`, the verb `unassign`): the others stand. A row that is not cancelled carries **«Dă-i rolul …»** while it holds none and **«Dă-i și rolul …»** once it holds some — one press per role ticked and not yet held, with how it stands, and «Alt rol» for the event's other roles not held — each adding that role beside those held (the verb `assign`, which no longer replaces). «Adaugă un voluntar de mână» and «Modifică» take «Rolurile date» as checkboxes, one per role (`assignedRoleIds`), the same shape as «Ce e dispus(ă) să facă»: any set, or none for a person still to place; at least one of the two groups, as before; a person entered with roles given and nothing ticked has those roles as their choices. **A person's full row stands once on the page**, under the first role given in the club's order; every other role's group lists them in one line — the name, the state and «vezi la …», a link to the row — so each group names everyone it counts and no form is drawn twice. Giving is audited as `volunteer.assigned` and taking back as `volunteer.unassigned`, each with the volunteer's id, the role's, the roles now held and those before; «Modifică» audits the field `assignedRoleIds`; a cancelled person is given no role (`CONFLICT`: reopen first), by any of the three; a press that changes nothing writes and sends nothing. Every writer still locks the event's roles first, in the order of their ids (§761's rule; «Ia-i rolul» too).

**Emails.** `VOLUNTEER_ROLE_ASSIGNED` names **every role that stands**, in one message, whichever press changed them — a role added, one taken back, the set ticked anew, roles kept while the address was corrected, a cancelled person with roles reopened — and is queued for no change that leaves none; its payload is the sorted set, and the send withdraws it when the person's roles are no longer that set. One role reads as §761 wrote it («Rol: …», «ți-au dat un rol», «Ce presupune rolul: …»); several read «Roluri: Punct de apă, Sosire», «Organizatorii ți-au dat mai multe roluri la …», «Ce presupune fiecare rol: Punct de apă — dai apă la km 5; Sosire — …» (the roles with no description adding nothing), English likewise; the footer names the contact person of every category concerned (§774), each once. The receipt's bold line says the roles given the same way.

**The agreement (§758, §761) — still the template's words.** `{{volunteerRole}}` takes the roles given by name, «Punct de apă, Sosire», and `{{volunteerTasks}}` what each asks by name — the shape the chosen roles' tasks already had — so the approved sentences read the same with one role or several; the chosen roles' blanks keep §761's rules while none is given. The link's page names the roles given joined by «, ». «Semnat pe hârtie» posts back the roles given, order-free (`roles:…`), and is refused (`VOLUNTEER_AGREEMENT_REPRINT`) when they changed; the card's «Contractul acceptat numește …» shows when the roles given no longer read as the accepted text named them — given exactly the roles it named, or only roles the person chose, still describes them.

**Everything else that said «the role given» says the roles.** The CSV's column is «Rolurile date», joined by «, », rows grouped by the first role given; the public list's card «Voluntarii» (§821) names a person's roles given joined by «, » — names only, as before; «Toate datele unei persoane» lists every role given beside every role ticked; the badges count a person on each role.

**Not changed:** the choices and the public form, the agreement's gates and acceptance, the privacy rules, the retention (the assignments go with the row), the event's JSON file (volunteers never travel), the capacity.

**Refused.** A flag on the choices' table (a role given is not a role offered: the organizers give roles the person never ticked, and the agreement's sentences name the two sets apart); counting a person once whatever they hold (they do each role; a role would look short-handed); the full row under every role given (the page would draw the same forms twice, with the same ids); dropping `role_id` in the same migration (expand and contract never share one, AGENTS.md §7.6; the code serving while it runs still reads it); a message per role (the person would read two emails for one decision, the second making the first wrong); replacing the roles on «Dă-i rolul» as before (the owner asked for several).

Amends §761 and §821.
changelogLine: - **A volunteer may be given several roles** — «Dă-i și rolul …» adds one beside those held, «Ia-i rolul …» on its chip takes one back, «Modifică» ticks «Rolurile date»; a person counts in each role's «N din M», the email names every role that stands, and the agreement, the CSV and the public list say them all. Migration 0177. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 136. Given the «Voluntari» card, then a volunteer may be given several roles: a row with none carries «Dă-i rolul …» and one with some «Dă-i și rolul …» — one press per role ticked and not held, naming how it stands, and «Alt rol» for the event's other roles not held — each adding that role beside those held; each role held is a chip under «Roluri date» with «Ia-i rolul …», which takes that one back and leaves the others; «Adaugă un voluntar de mână» and «Modifică» take «Rolurile date» as one checkbox per role, any set or none; a person counts against each role given («N din M», the public form's count and «Câte ecusoane» alike); their full row stands once, under the first role given in the club's order, and each other role's group lists them in one line «vezi la …» linking to it; giving is audited as `volunteer.assigned` and taking back as `volunteer.unassigned`, each with the role, the roles now held and those before; a cancelled person is given no role by any of the three; a role anybody holds or ticked is not deleted; the CSV's column «Rolurile date» joins them by «, », its rows grouped by the first; migration `0177_volunteer_role_assignments` is expand-only — the table `event_volunteer_role_assignments` (the choices' shape and cascades), each existing `role_id` its one row, `role_id` itself untouched and mirrored by every later write as the first role given until its contract release (2026-10-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 43. Given a change of the roles given to a volunteer — a role added, one taken back, the set ticked anew in «Modifică», roles kept while the address is corrected, or a cancelled person with roles reopened — then one `VOLUNTEER_ROLE_ASSIGNED` is queued naming every role that stands, none when none stands, with the sorted set as its payload; it reads as before for one role and «Roluri: …», «Organizatorii ți-au dat mai multe roluri la …» and «Ce presupune fiecare rol: … — …; … — …» for several (English likewise), its footer naming the contact of every category concerned; it is withdrawn at the send when the person's roles are no longer that set (2026-10-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 67. Given several roles given, then `{{volunteerRole}}` holds their names joined by «, » and `{{volunteerTasks}}` what each asks by name, «Punct de apă — …; Sosire — …», under any text; «Semnat pe hârtie» posts back the roles given, order-free, and is refused when they changed since the print; the card's «Contractul acceptat numește …» shows only when the roles given no longer read as the accepted text named them (2026-10-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 56. Given a volunteer named on the event page's card «Voluntarii», then the role beside the name is every role given, joined by «, » in the page's language — names only, as before (2026-10-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
Amends criterion 10. «Toate datele unei persoane» lists every role given, joined by «, », beside every role ticked (2026-10-20, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
